{{Short description|Italian mathematician (1716-1787)}}

[[File:Marzagaglia, Gaetano – Del calcolo balistico, 1748 – BEIC 11380801.jpg|thumb|''Del calcolo balistico'' (1748)]]

'''Gaetano Marzagaglia''', or '''Marzagalia''' or '''Marcegaglia''' ([[Chiampo]], 7 August 1716 – [[Verona]], 1 July 1787), was an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[Catholic priest]].<ref name="DBI">{{Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/gaetano-marzagaglia_(Dizionario-Biografico)/|author=Ivano Dal Prete|title=Marzagaglia, Gaetano|volume=71}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://data.cerl.org/thesaurus/cnp00994202|title=Marzagalia, Gaetano|publisher=[[Consortium of European Research Libraries]]|access-date=2026-05-18}}</ref>

Marzagaglia was an advocate of the applications of mathematics and its importance in society. He directed the episcopal seminary of Verona from 1760 to 1772.<ref name="DBI" />

He refuted the theses of [[Giuseppe Suzzi]] in ''Lettera di un matematico italiano'' ("Letter of an Italian Mathematician"). In ''Dimostrazioni algebriche'' ("Algebraic Demonstrations"), he replied to a pamphlet by [[Francesco Ventretti]].<ref name="DBI" />
